title: E² Core Framework relationship graph
description: Navigation graph for the public corpus. Curated edges are orientation metadata, while suggested edges come from exact title mentions and are not framework authority.

authority.relationships: Navigation metadata only; consult the linked documents for authority

clusters.name: Foundational Axioms & Core Ontology
clusters.scope: The irreducible bedrock of E². Establishes what relationships *are*, how they compose, and what constraints govern all relational systems. Every other cluster presupposes this one.

clusters.name: Formal, Mathematical & Epistemic Constraints
clusters.scope: Formal mappings of E² into established mathematical formalisms, together with the epistemic conditions and limits governing what the framework may defensibly claim. Covers category theory, lambda calculus, relational physics, computability, embedded universality, and predictive lawfulness.

clusters.name: Dynamics, Emergence & Systems Frameworks
clusters.scope: How relational systems change, stabilize, route flow, maintain continuity, resolve possibility, and generate emergent structure. Covers boundary dynamics, flow operators, resolution, persistence, CFA/CFAR, AVIA, REMF, emergence simulation, and tensional intelligence.

clusters.name: Metabolic, Resonance & Temporal Physics
clusters.scope: The physics of meaning-making and temporal dynamics. Metabolic Meaning treats meaning as a metabolic process with a phase space topology. Resonance frameworks map coherence across ontological scales. TCL documents formalize temporal constraint coupling constants.

clusters.name: Ethics, Stewardship, Accountability & Rights
clusters.scope: The normative and answerability layer of E². Grounds rights, stewardship, trust, custody, accountability, consequence routing, and repair in relational structure. Localization and typed-condition work make assignment inspectable within complex causal chains. Includes temporal ethics and AI interaction ethics.

clusters.name: Adversarial, Security & Cognitive Integrity
clusters.scope: How relational systems resist, detect, and recover from adversarial manipulation. AOMI formalizes mechanism gaming and Goodhart dynamics; MRIE addresses identity-pattern exposure through relational signatures; the Exposure Protocol preserves coherence during transmission.

clusters.name: Consciousness, Cognition & Identity
clusters.scope: How relational dynamics give rise to consciousness, cognitive structure, selfhood, and identity. Treats consciousness as triadic relational architecture, the self as a six-primitive coherence field, intelligence as field navigation, and cognition as collective substrate. Distinct from [F](#cluster-f "symmetric:constrains") (which addresses threats to cognitive integrity) and from [H](#cluster-h "dynamical:produces") (which applies these to social systems).

clusters.name: Social, Civilizational & Applied
clusters.scope: E² applied to human social systems: families, care economies, power dynamics, civilization, and collective substrate. Includes manifestos and applied frameworks for transformation. Covers communication theory as a social application.

clusters.name: Protocol, Infrastructure & Meta
clusters.scope: The operational layer — how the Context Layer itself is structured, transmitted, and versioned. CLP defines the data model governing all other clusters; RPE is the simulation engine for relational primitives; Implementations is the living registry of E² applications.
